findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies a binding with a changed baseline field IS written (and produces a commit) after the guard is introduced, covering the positive path of the write-when-changed logic.
evidence: AC#1 tests 'unchanged Jira state → byte-identical file and no commit' (negative/idempotence path only)
Approach: 'build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal' — the non-early-return (write) path has no covering criterion
ABSENCE: no AC asserts that a binding whose baseline genuinely changed is still persisted after the guard is introduced
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion validates the write-when-changed guard's positive path — i.e., that when baseline values DO change, set_baseline still writes the updated baseline. All ACs test the 'no change → no write' case; the 'change → write' case is an uncovered deliverable.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria section — all five ACs
scenarios: An implementer who always returns early (never writes) would pass all five ACs while silently dropping baseline updates when real Jira edits arrive — the exact regression the guard is meant to prevent once 'real Jira edits arrive' (per Approach).
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] When one binding's baseline value changes between passes, set_baseline writes the updated entry and a commit is produced. Tier: integration or unit against set_baseline with a pre-existing entry that differs from the new baseline.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-time migration step (or specify that `set_baseline` strips `baseline_advanced_at` from existing entries on first read/write regardless of the write-when-changed guard) so that the field is fully retired from persisted data, and extend AC #2 to assert absence in written file content, not just source code.
evidence: AC #2: 'grep -rn baseline_advanced_at src/ returns nothing' — this verifies source code only, not persisted file content.
'return early if equal' — entries whose baseline never changes will never be rewritten, so the old field persists in those records indefinitely.
Plan states field is 'written in exactly one place and read nowhere in src/' — correct for new code, but does not address existing data already on disk.
findings.finding: The plan specifies that `baseline_advanced_at` will no longer be written by `set_baseline`, but it does not define a RETIRE/cleanup path for the field in *already-persisted* `bindings.json` entries. Because the write-when-changed guard prevents any write when the baseline is unchanged, pre-existing entries whose baseline never changes after upgrade will retain `baseline_advanced_at` in the file indefinitely. AC #2 only checks `src/` source code, not live data, so this stale-field accumulation goes undetected by any specified acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #2; Approach section ('build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal')
scenarios: A user upgrades rebar against an existing `bindings.json` that contains many entries with `baseline_advanced_at`. Those entries are never touched by the write-when-changed guard (baselines unchanged), so the field accumulates permanently in the file. Any downstream tooling, audit, or schema validator that inspects persisted data will still observe `baseline_advanced_at` long after the upgrade, and the marginal packed cost reduction may be smaller than projected for repos with a large proportion of stable-baseline entries.
findings.suggested_fix: In `set_baseline`, after loading the existing entry, unconditionally `pop('baseline_advanced_at', None)` from the entry dict before the equality comparison. This ensures the field is removed on the next write of each entry regardless of whether the baseline value itself changed, providing a natural migration pass with zero extra I/O.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-shot migration step (or a lazy-scrub on first save() after upgrade) that removes `baseline_advanced_at` from all already-persisted `bindings.json` entries, and document the post-rollback schema state (stale entries will re-accumulate the field on first set_baseline call after rollback — confirm this is acceptable).
evidence: Plan states the field is 'written in exactly one place and read nowhere in src/' — implies stale copies in persisted entries are invisible to runtime but still bloat git pack objects
AC #5 requires '(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)' measurement across N>=40 consecutive revisions, but stale baseline_advanced_at keys remain in entries not touched by set_baseline during that window
Plan's Approach section only says 'never write baseline_advanced_at' in set_baseline — no scrub of existing entries is mentioned
ABSENCE: no migration step in 'Files' list or Approach to iterate over existing bindings and delete the key
findings.finding: The plan does not include a one-shot migration pass to strip `baseline_advanced_at` from already-persisted `bindings.json` entries. New code stops writing the field, but existing entries retain the stale key until they are naturally touched by `set_baseline`. This means the headline 7.4x pack-size savings (AC #5) accrue only to entries rewritten after deployment, not the full file — and the AC #5 measurement protocol (N>=40 consecutive revisions rebuilt from a live repo) may pass or fail depending on how many existing entries happen to be touched in the window, making the acceptance criterion partially untestable without a scrub.
scenarios: Deployment lands; 600 existing bound entries all carry baseline_advanced_at; over 40 passes only a small fraction of entries have their baseline touched; pack-size measurement shows only modest improvement, not the claimed 7.4x, and AC #5 fails.

Engineer running the AC #5 measurement on a repo where Jira is quiescent (0 changes/pass, per the plan's own data) observes that set_baseline is never called at all for non-adopted entries, so zero entries are scrubbed and the stale field persists indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: In `BindingStore.save()` or a dedicated `migrate_v2_to_v3()` method called on `load()`, iterate `self._data['bindings'].values()` and `del entry['baseline_advanced_at']` where present (idempotent). This ensures the first `save()` after upgrade produces a fully-scrubbed file and AC #5 is measurable from day 1. Document that rollback to old code re-stamps the field only on entries subsequently touched by set_baseline (no data loss, bounded regression).
